sentences.text: Rapetosaurus was a four-legged dinosaur that ate plants.
This animal possessed a bulky body, a long neck, and a short, thin tail typical of sauropods.
Its head featured a long, narrow snout with nostrils located on the top of the skull, resembling diplodocids.
Small, pencil-like teeth were adapted for stripping leaves from trees rather than chewing them.
The skull also displayed an elongated snout and two narrow openings on the top surface.
The juvenile skeleton found is the most complete titanosaur ever discovered and the only one with the head still attached to the body.
This young individual weighed around 40 kilograms and was likely between 39 and 77 days old when it died.
At the time of hatching, a juvenile Rapetosaurus was estimated to weigh 3.4 kilograms.
Rapetosaurus was atypical among titanosaurs because it shared the Mahajanga basin with only one other large herbivore, another titanosaurian.
Smaller herbivores were rare, and only one species, Simosuchus, was discovered during more than 100 years of collection in that area.
Rapetosaurus was the first titanosaur ever discovered with an almost perfectly intact skeleton that included a skull.
The discovery included a nearly complete juvenile skeleton and partial remains from three other individuals.
The discovery was published in 2001 by Kristina Curry Rogers and Catherine A. Forster in the scientific journal Nature.
Kristina Curry Rogers and her colleagues discovered a rare juvenile Rapetosaurus specimen in a museum collection.
There are 5 recorded fossil occurrences of Rapetosaurus.
Analysis of bone remodeling suggests juvenile Rapetosaurus could survive with little to no parental care.
Evidence suggests a juvenile Rapetosaurus likely died of starvation caused by harsh droughts in Cretaceous Madagascar.
Tooth marks on Rapetosaurus bones indicate that the predator Majungasaurus fed on this sauropod.
Scientists suggest that Majungasaurus specialized in hunting sauropods.
Tooth marks of Majungasaurus on Rapetosaurus bones indicate that it at least fed on these sauropods, whether it killed them or not.
Due to the absence of ornithischian dinosaurs, it is suggested that prehistoric Madagascar saw a different herbivore community dynamic than other parts of the Cretaceous.
In 2020, Molina-Pérez and Larramendi estimated the size of the probable adult specimen MAD 93-18, known from a femur, at 16.5 meters and 10.3 tonnes.
Adult Rapetosaurus reached a length of about 15 meters, which is less than half the size of other giant titanosaurs like Argentinosaurus.
Rapetosaurus is classified within the family Saltasauridae.
Rapetosaurus is a member of the Subfamily Nemegtosaurinae within Saltasauridae, belonging to the unranked clade Titanosauria.
Rapetosaurus belongs to the parent group Saltasauroidea.
Rapetosaurus krausei is the only known species in the extinct genus Rapetosaurus.
During the Maastrichtian, Madagascar was an island that had separated from the Indian subcontinent less than 20 million years prior.
The climate in Madagascar during the Maastrichtian was semi-arid with strong seasonal variations in temperature and rainfall.
Fossilized remains were found in the Mahajanga Basin in northwestern Madagascar, not far from the port city of Mahajanga.
Analysis of the skull and body confirmed the speculative hypothesis that titanosaurs are more closely related to brachiosaurids.
